for_the_reviewer:
Press first on the Hume half of the coverage.md sentence. Fault 22 named Meno and said 'this one adjacency'; I ran the same check (17 new sources against the old rig's 49 and file 50's table, on url, title and author/translator surname) and it returns two of the same kind: W7 Euthyphro ~ P7 Meno (Plato, both Jowett) and W8 Dialogues ~ P2 Enquiry (both Hume). Naming one and leaving the other out would fail the test the fault applies, so I named both and wrote two sentences rather than one, in the shape the Hilbert/Michelson lines already use. If you judge the Hume half out of the fault's scope, strike that clause; the Meno half is the forced fix and stands alone.

Second, the falsifier for fault 21 is worth keeping in the record, because it says which spelling is load-bearing. With sources.json as frozen (curly), arm (x) on W9 replaces 39 and 27. Put split.json's straight form into sources.json and it replaces 0 and 27 - exchange.py marks the run 'void' for that name. So the tempting other repair (make sources.json match split.json) would silently empty half of arm (x) on W9. Nothing reads split.json's exchange field, which is why the addendum is a line and not an edit.

Third, something I found and did not touch, because no fault of mine names it: dry/ under the harness holds another agent's prompt files for W1 that carry the corpus document text (dry/sonnet/prompts/W1-*/*.txt, 47 KB each). The harness .gitignore is 'dry/', so nothing is committed, but coverage.md section 0 and fetch.py both say the text is never kept in the repository, and a working tree that holds it reads against that. Your call whether the rule is about the commit or the folder; I deleted my own W9 dry output so nothing of mine is there.

Fourth, the two documents for your dry run are already fetched and hash-checked at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ThreadSmith/00bda300-7321-5714-a655-4358c87aab9b/scratchpad/w10texts (W1.txt, W9.txt), outside the repository. `python3 fetch.py W1 W9 --check` reproduces both hashes from the addresses today.

Fifth, what I could not settle: whether 'in Jowett's translation' is true of the old rig's P7 by anything stronger than the record's own returns. The old manifest gives author 'Plato' and no translator; what I have is that one P7 report is headed "Plato's *Meno* (Jowett translation)" and another argues with Jowett's introduction, and that the old fetcher took the first 14,000 words of the Gutenberg file with no start marker. I did not fetch pg1643 to look, because the task allows the corpus fetcher and the corpus documents only. If you want that claim *seen* rather than read off the returns, fetching epub 1643 once would settle it.
